_comment: AEGIS Destructive Command Rules — append-only. Never remove entries. Add new ones as threats discovered.
_reason: 5 database wipes in production. This file defines what agents can NEVER do without human override. 2026-08-01: +2 Prisma shadow-database patterns — the wiper that wears the safety tool's name (see those entries' reason fields). 2026-10-02: two patterns narrowed, none removed — each still refuses every statement form in tests/shipped-ruleset.test.ts, and refuses nothing it did not refuse before. 2026-10-05: gaps in five patterns bounded and the compose rule made to name the subcommand, none removed; the override token is gone (KAV-098).

bash_block_patterns.reason: Drops entire database — data loss is permanent

Drops table — schema and data loss (2026-10-02: narrowed — what follows must be able to begin a table name; a match followed only by punctuation such as . , ; | / ( ) or a dash is prose, not a statement)
Drops schema — all tables in schema lost

Truncates table — deletes all rows instantly, no WAL (2026-10-02: narrowed — the shell tool's flag form `truncate -s …` and a keyword followed only by punctuation no longer match; a quoted, variable or bare table name still does)
dropdb CLI — drops entire PostgreSQL database
prisma migrate reset drops all tables; prisma db push can silently drop columns
compose down/rm with the volumes flag removes volumes — permanent data loss
Removes Docker volumes — permanent data loss
Stops PostgreSQL cluster — interrupts all services
Stops/disables PostgreSQL service — all 5 clusters offline
SQL DELETE — removes rows. Use soft-delete (deleted_at) pattern instead.
Drops column — schema change with data loss
pg_restore --clean drops objects before recreating — wipe risk

Prisma RESETS the shadow database before replaying migrations onto it — aim it at a live DB and the reset IS the wipe, executed inside Prisma, never appearing as a DROP in the command. This is the 2026-07-30 public incident: `prisma migrate diff --from-migrations ... --shadow-database-url <PROD>` emptied all 22 tables of a live Supabase DB. ANKR needs no shadow DB anywhere: R-010 uses --from-schema-datasource and ankr-db-guard.sh uses --from-url, both read-only introspection. Zero occurrences in the tree as of 2026-08-01, so this blocks nothing that exists.

The ONLY forms of `prisma migrate diff` that are not read-only. --from-migrations/--to-migrations must replay a migrations folder onto a real database, so Prisma requires a shadow DB and resets it first. Every other diff form (--from-url, --from-schema-datasource, --from-empty) touches nothing. Use those.
rm -rf of / (root) — catastrophic filesystem wipe. Anchored to root only: `rm -rf /tmp/x` or `rm -rf ./node_modules` do NOT match (2026-09-24, AF-R-001, from retired format-A DES-014).
chmod 777 — world-writable permissions, a security risk (2026-09-24, AF-R-001, from retired format-A DES-012).

chown -R on / — recursive ownership change of the root filesystem, possible system damage (2026-09-24, AF-R-001, from retired format-A DES-013). NOT added (AF-R-001): `> /dev/null` (mass false positives), `kill/killall` (ankr-ctl friction), `truncate -s 0` (the shell `truncate` command is already caught, over-broadly but safely, by the SQL `TRUNCATE\s+` rule above).

override_instructions: Nothing typed into a command overrides these rules. When a command is refused the gate prints a code; a person runs `aegis approve-destructive <code>` in their own terminal, and the same command then goes through once, within ten minutes.
_note: No text in a command overrides these rules. A person approves one refused command, once: aegis approve-destructive <code> (KAV-098).
